contexts.text: For a man can act the sycophant both in civil and moral things, and in spiritual ones.

Hence every man who is not led by the Lord interiorly is a pretender, a sycophant, a hypocrite; and thus an apparent man... of whom it may be said that his shell or body is wise, and his kernel or spirit insane...
Man's will is twofold... and therefore a sycophant can act and speak before the world in one way, and with his familiars in another...
It is like a pious sycophant.
The interiors of their minds are infernal, and the exteriors are as it were heavenly from a feigned morality; for they are sycophants and hypocrites.
